ov: Small, round, tailless relatives of rabbits with short, rounded ears, living on rocky mountain slopes in Asia and North America. They do not hibernate; instead they spend summer gathering "haypiles" of plants to eat in winter. Their high alarm call earned them the name whistling hare.
rg: Cold mountains and steppes of Asia and western North America; the large-eared pika lives above 6,000 m in the Himalayas.
df: Grasses, flowers, sedges, shrub twigs, moss and lichens.
fx: An American pika can make over 100 trips a day to build its haypile.
For every 1 °C rise in temperature, pikas lose about 3% of their foraging time.
